name: Common Garter Snake
habitat: Almost anywhere damp: meadows, marshes, stream banks, woodland edges, parks and gardens
range: Across most of North America, from the Atlantic to the Pacific and from Florida to the Northwest Territories; the most widespread snake on the continent
diet: Earthworms, frogs, toads, salamanders, fish and slugs
active: By day; active even in cool weather
ids: Three pale stripes, yellow, green or blue, one down the back and one along each lower side, on a dark body.
The side stripes sit on the second and third rows of scales above the belly.
Often a checkerboard of dark spots between the stripes, and red or orange flecks on the sides in many areas.
Keeled scales, a slim body and round pupils.

look.colour: Black, brown, olive or green, with yellow, green or blue stripes
look.pattern: Three stripes, often with dark checks between
look.head: Slightly wider than the neck, with pale lips

fact: In Manitoba, tens of thousands crawl out of the same limestone dens each spring, the largest gatherings of snakes on Earth.

name: Western Terrestrial Garter Snake
habitat: Meadows, streams, lakes, sagebrush and forest clearings, up into high mountains
range: Western North America: British Columbia and Alberta south through the Rockies, Great Basin and California to New Mexico
diet: Slugs, frogs, fish, small mammals, lizards and leeches
ids: A pale yellow or cream stripe down the back, often dull or wavy, and a pale stripe along each side.
Dark spots between the stripes; some snakes are mostly dark.
Keeled scales and a fairly broad head.

look.colour: Brown, grey or olive with yellow stripes
look.pattern: Three stripes with dark spots between
look.head: Broad, wider than the neck

fact: Its saliva is mildly toxic to small prey; a bite can cause a little local swelling in people but is not dangerous.

name: Western Ribbonsnake
habitat: Edges of ponds, marshes, streams and wet meadows
range: The central USA from Wisconsin and Indiana to Louisiana, Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas and New Mexico; into Mexico
diet: Frogs, tadpoles, toads and small fish
ids: Very slender, with a long tail about a third of its length.
A bright orange or yellow stripe down the back and yellow side stripes on a black or brown body.
Plain, unmarked pale lips, and a white mark in front of the eye.
Keeled scales and large eyes.

look.colour: Black or brown with an orange or yellow back stripe
look.head: Narrow, with plain pale lips
look.body: Very slender, with a long tail

fact: Ribbonsnakes often flee across the surface of the water and into vegetation rather than diving.

name: Northwestern Garter Snake
habitat: Meadows, forest clearings, gardens and coastal thickets
range: The Pacific north-west: south-western British Columbia, western Washington and Oregon, and north-western California
ids: Small and very variable: the back stripe can be red, orange, yellow, blue or missing.
Dark brown, black or green body.
A small head and keeled scales.

look.colour: Brown, black or green; stripes red, orange, yellow or blue
look.head: Small and narrow

fact: It is the slug-eating garter snake of Pacific north-west gardens.

name: Eastern Ribbonsnake
habitat: Edges of ponds, marshes, bogs, streams and wet meadows
range: The eastern USA from Maine and southern Ontario to Florida, west to Wisconsin and Louisiana; Nova Scotia
diet: Frogs, tadpoles, salamanders and small fish
ids: Very slender with a long tail, about a third of its length.
Three bright yellow stripes on a black or dark brown body.
Plain pale lips and a pale crescent in front of the eye.

look.colour: Black or dark brown with yellow stripes
look.head: Narrow, with plain lips
look.body: Very slender, with a long tail

fact: It is told from the Common Garter Snake by its slimmer build, longer tail and unmarked lips.

name: Plains Garter Snake
habitat: Wet prairie, marshes, pond edges and vacant lots, even in cities
range: The Great Plains and Midwest, from Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba to Illinois, Colorado, Kansas and New Mexico
diet: Earthworms, frogs, salamanders and small fish
ids: A bright yellow or orange stripe down the back and pale stripes on the sides.
The side stripes sit on the third and fourth rows of scales near the head.
Two rows of dark spots between the stripes and black bars on the lips.

look.colour: Black or olive with yellow or orange stripes
look.head: With black bars on the lips

fact: It is one of the snakes most likely to be found in city parks in Chicago and Denver.

name: Checkered Garter Snake
habitat: Streams, ditches, ponds and irrigated land in dry country
range: The south-west and southern plains: Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and south-eastern California; into Mexico
diet: Frogs, toads, tadpoles, fish and earthworms
active: At dusk and night in hot weather, by day otherwise
ids: A bold black checkerboard pattern on an olive or tan body.
A pale back stripe and pale side stripes.
A pale crescent behind the corner of the mouth, followed by a dark blotch.

look.head: With a pale crescent and dark blotch behind the jaw

fact: It manages to live in deserts by following irrigation ditches and stock tanks.

name: Aquatic Garter Snake
habitat: Streams, ponds and coastal creeks in grassland and woodland
range: Coastal California and south-western Oregon
ids: A yellow or orange stripe down the back, with a dark body; the throat is often bright yellow.
Side stripes are faint or missing in some areas.
Keeled scales and a narrow head.

look.colour: Dark olive or black; back stripe yellow or orange
look.head: Narrow, with a yellow throat

fact: It dives readily and hunts fish under water.

name: Black-necked Garter Snake
habitat: Rocky streams, canyons and ponds in mountains and desert grassland
range: The south-west: Utah, Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas; into Mexico
ids: Two large black blotches on the neck behind a grey head.
A yellow or orange stripe down the back and pale side stripes.
Dark checks between the stripes.

look.pattern: Stripes with dark checks; black neck blotches
look.head: Grey, with black patches behind it

fact: It often hunts tadpoles in drying pools along desert streams.

name: Two-striped Garter Snake
habitat: Streams, pools and ponds with dense plants along the banks
range: Coastal and southern California; into Baja California
ids: Usually no stripe down the back: just a pale yellow stripe along each side.
Olive, brown or grey body with small dark spots.
Some snakes are almost plain dark.

look.pattern: Two pale side stripes, no back stripe
look.head: Narrow

fact: Its lack of a back stripe sets it apart from almost every other garter snake.

name: Sierra Garter Snake
habitat: Rocky streams, rivers and lakes in the Sierra Nevada and Cascades
range: California and western Nevada
ids: Dark olive or brown with a checkerboard of dark blotches.
The back stripe is faint or missing; side stripes are dull.
A narrow, pointed head.
fact: It hunts fish and tadpoles under water among stream boulders.

name: Butler's Garter Snake
habitat: Wet meadows, prairie, marsh edges and vacant lots
range: Around the Great Lakes: Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Wisconsin and southern Ontario
ids: Small, with a small head barely wider than the neck.
Three yellow or orange stripes; the side stripes are on the third row of scales.
Wriggles from side to side when picked up instead of biting.

look.colour: Black or dark olive with yellow stripes
look.head: Very small

fact: Its tiny head is the best clue that it is not a young Common Garter Snake.

name: Short-headed Garter Snake
habitat: Old fields, meadows and stream edges
range: North-western Pennsylvania and south-western New York; introduced near Pittsburgh and in Ohio
ids: A very small head, no wider than the neck.
Three yellow or tan stripes on a brown body.
Small and slim.
fact: Almost its whole world range lies within the Allegheny Plateau.

name: Giant Garter Snake
habitat: Marshes, sloughs, rice fields and irrigation canals
range: The Central Valley of California
ids: The largest garter snake: long and heavy-bodied.
Dark brown or olive with a yellow back stripe and checkered dark spots.
Keeled scales and a long head.

look.colour: Dark brown or olive with a yellow back stripe
look.head: Long and narrow

fact: Most of its marsh habitat is gone; it now survives largely in rice fields.

name: Narrow-headed Garter Snake
habitat: Clear rocky streams in pine and oak forest
range: Central and eastern Arizona and western New Mexico
ids: Olive or tan with rows of dark brown or reddish spots; no stripes.
A long, narrow, pointed head with eyes set high.
Keeled scales.

look.pattern: Rows of dark spots, no stripes
look.head: Long, narrow and pointed

fact: It hunts fish among stream boulders and is threatened by introduced crayfish and bass.

name: Common Watersnake
habitat: Lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, marshes and canals
range: Eastern and central North America, from southern Ontario and Quebec to the Gulf coast and west to Colorado
ids: Brown or grey with dark crossbands on the front of the body that break into alternating blotches towards the tail.
Often looks plain dark when dry and muddy.
A belly with reddish or black half-moons.
Round pupils and keeled scales; flattens its body and bites hard if grabbed.
fact: It is the snake most often mistaken for a cottonmouth or copperhead, though it is harmless.

name: Plain-bellied Watersnake
habitat: Rivers, swamps, ponds, lakes and wet woodland; wanders far from water
range: The south-east and south-central USA, from Delaware and Michigan to Florida, west to Kansas and Texas; into Mexico
ids: Plain brown, grey or olive above, with no clear pattern.
A plain, unmarked belly: red, orange or yellow.
Young snakes are boldly blotched.

look.colour: Plain brown, grey or olive; belly red, orange or yellow
look.head: Broad, with round pupils

fact: It is more of a frog-eater than other watersnakes and often wanders through woods between ponds.

name: Banded Watersnake
habitat: Marshes, swamps, ponds, lakes, ditches and canals
range: The south-eastern coastal plain from North Carolina to Florida, west to Texas, and up the Mississippi to Illinois
ids: Dark crossbands run the whole length of the body, on a grey, tan, red or yellowish background.
A dark stripe from the eye to the corner of the jaw.
A belly with dark squares or wavy marks.

look.colour: Grey, tan, red or yellow with dark bands
look.head: With a dark stripe from eye to jaw

fact: The Florida form is often bright red or orange and is often confused with cottonmouths.

name: Diamond-backed Watersnake
habitat: Rivers, lakes, ponds, bayous and swamps
range: The Mississippi valley and Gulf states: Illinois and Indiana to Louisiana, Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas; into Mexico
ids: A dark net-like pattern that leaves pale diamond-shaped patches along the back.
Brown, olive or yellowish, with a yellow belly marked with dark half-moons.
A large, heavy watersnake.

look.pattern: Dark chain-like net with pale diamonds
look.head: Broad

fact: It is often called a "water moccasin" and killed, though it is harmless.

name: Brown Watersnake
habitat: Rivers, cypress swamps, lakes and canals; basks on branches over the water
range: The south-eastern coastal plain: Virginia to Florida and Alabama
ids: Brown, with large dark squarish blotches down the back and alternating ones on the sides.
A wide head that is distinctly broader than the neck.
Heavy body with keeled scales.
fact: It basks on branches high above the water and drops in when disturbed.

name: Florida Green Watersnake
habitat: Marshes, lakes, swamps, ditches and canals with dense plants
range: Florida, south-eastern Georgia and the coastal Carolinas
ids: Large and heavy, plain olive-green or brown with faint dark bars.
A row of small scales below the eye (most watersnakes have none).
A pale, mostly unmarked belly.

look.head: Broad, with small scales under the eye

fact: It is one of the largest watersnakes in North America.

name: Salt Marsh Snake
habitat: Salt and brackish marshes, mangroves and tidal flats
range: Gulf and Atlantic coasts from Texas to Florida
ids: On the Gulf coast: four dark stripes on a tan or grey body.
In Florida mangroves: banded or plain, often reddish.
A small watersnake that lives in salt water.
fact: It does not drink salt water; it waits for rain and drinks fresh water from the surface.

name: Mississippi Green Watersnake
habitat: Swamps, marshes, bayous and slow rivers
range: The lower Mississippi valley and Gulf coast: Illinois to Louisiana, Texas and Alabama
ids: Olive-green or brown with faint dark bars.
A row of small scales between the eye and the lip scales.
A dark belly with pale half-moon spots.

look.head: Broad, with small scales under the eye

fact: It and the Florida Green Watersnake are the only North American watersnakes with scales beneath the eye.

name: Brazos Watersnake
habitat: Rocky shallows and riffles of rivers
range: Only the upper Brazos River basin in north-central Texas
ids: A small watersnake, light brown or olive with rows of alternating dark spots.
A pinkish or orange belly.
Keeled scales.
fact: It lives in a single river system and is one of the rarest snakes in the USA.

name: Queen Snake
habitat: Clean, rocky streams and rivers with plenty of crayfish
range: The eastern USA from Pennsylvania and southern Ontario to the Florida panhandle, west to Wisconsin and Arkansas
ids: Brown or olive, with a yellow stripe along each lower side.
A yellow belly with four brown stripes running along it.
Slim, with keeled scales.
fact: It eats almost nothing but soft crayfish that have just shed their shells.

name: Graham's Crayfish Snake
habitat: Ponds, marshes, ditches and slow streams in prairie
range: The Mississippi valley and plains: Iowa and Illinois to Louisiana, Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas
ids: A broad yellow stripe along each lower side, below a dark brown back.
A plain yellow belly.
A narrow, small head.

look.colour: Dark brown with yellow side stripes
look.head: Narrow and small

fact: It hides in crayfish burrows and comes out to hunt on warm, wet nights.

name: Striped Crayfish Snake
habitat: Marshes, lakes and ditches thick with water hyacinth and other floating plants
range: Florida and southern Georgia
ids: Glossy brown with three faint dark stripes and a pale yellowish stripe low on each side.
Smooth, shiny scales.
A yellow or orange belly, sometimes with dark spots.
fact: It has specially hinged teeth for gripping the hard shells of crayfish.

name: Glossy Crayfish Snake
habitat: Swamps, marshes and slow streams
range: The Gulf and Atlantic coastal plain from Virginia to Florida and Texas
ids: Glossy brown with faint darker stripes.
A yellow belly with two rows of dark spots.
Smooth, shiny scales.
fact: It is so secretive that it is mostly found by searching wetland plants at night.

name: Black Swampsnake
habitat: Swamps, marshes, ponds and wet ditches, among floating plants
range: The coastal plain of the Carolinas, Georgia, Florida and Alabama
diet: Small fish, tadpoles, salamanders and leeches
ids: Small and glossy black above.
A bright red or orange belly.
Smooth, shiny scales.
fact: It can survive droughts by waiting out the dry season in mud and crayfish burrows.

name: DeKay's Brownsnake
habitat: Gardens, parks, vacant lots, woodland and wet meadows; common in cities
range: Eastern North America from southern Quebec and Ontario to Florida, west to Minnesota and Texas; into Mexico
ids: A small brown or grey snake with two rows of small dark spots down the back, often joined by thin lines.
A paler band along the spine.
A dark mark on the side of the head and neck; keeled scales.

look.pattern: Two rows of small dark spots
look.head: Small, with a dark mark behind the eye

fact: It thrives in city lots and backyards, eating the slugs that gardeners dislike.

name: Red-bellied Snake
habitat: Woodland, forest clearings, bogs and meadows
range: Eastern North America from Nova Scotia and Saskatchewan to Florida and east Texas
ids: A tiny snake, brown, grey or black above with a bright red or orange belly.
Three pale spots on the back of the neck, often joined into a collar.
Keeled scales and a small head.

look.colour: Brown, grey or black above; red belly
look.pattern: Plain or faint stripes; pale neck spots
look.head: Small, with a pale nape

fact: When frightened it curls its upper lip to show its teeth, a bluff it never follows through.

name: Florida Brownsnake
habitat: Marshes, wet prairie, pine flatwoods and under debris
range: Florida and south Georgia
ids: A tiny grey-brown snake with a pale band across the back of the head.
A pale back stripe and small dark spots.
Keeled scales.

look.pattern: Pale back band; small dark spots
look.head: Small, with a pale band behind it

fact: It was treated as a form of DeKay's Brownsnake until 2006.

name: Rough Earthsnake
habitat: Woodland, gardens and fields, under leaf litter, logs and stones
range: The south-east and south-central USA, from Virginia and Florida to Kansas and Texas
ids: A tiny, plain brown or grey snake with a pointed snout.
Keeled scales and often a faint pale band across the back of the head.
A plain cream belly.
fact: It is one of the snakes most often dug up in gardens and flowerbeds in Texas.

name: Smooth Earthsnake
habitat: Damp woodland, under leaf litter, logs and stones
range: The eastern USA from New Jersey to Florida, west to Iowa and Texas
ids: A tiny, plain grey or light brown snake, sometimes with faint black specks on the back.
Smooth or only faintly ridged scales.
A small, rounded head.
fact: It spends nearly all its life hidden under logs and in loose soil.

name: Lined Snake
habitat: Prairie, vacant lots, parks and gardens; often in towns
range: The Great Plains and Midwest: from South Dakota and Illinois to Texas, Kansas, Colorado and New Mexico
active: At night; under cover by day
ids: Looks like a small garter snake: grey-brown with a pale stripe down the back and one on each side.
Two rows of bold black half-moons along the belly.
A small head and keeled scales.

look.pattern: Three pale stripes; black half-moons on the belly
look.head: Small

fact: The double row of black half-moons on its belly tells it apart from garter snakes.

name: Kirtland's Snake
habitat: Wet meadows, prairie fens, marsh edges and city lots near water
range: The Midwest: Indiana, Ohio, Illinois, Kentucky, Michigan and Pennsylvania
active: Mostly at night; often in crayfish burrows
ids: Small, grey-brown with four rows of round dark blotches.
A bright red or pink belly with a row of black dots along each edge.
Flattens its body to look bigger when threatened.
fact: It is a rare snake of Midwestern wet prairies, many of which have been drained.
